edges.description: Reduced WNT7A signalling from dorsal ectoderm weakens induction of the dorsal mesenchymal programme.
edges.target: Impaired Dorsoventral Patterning of the Limb

edges.description: WNT7A is required to sustain Shh in the posterior mesenchyme, so partial loss compromises anteroposterior patterning as well.
Nails are dorsal appendages; loss of dorsal identity leaves them hypoplastic.
edges.source: Impaired Dorsoventral Patterning of the Limb

edges.description: Loss of posterior skeletal elements manifests as fibular aplasia and oligodactyly.

nodes.description: Dorsal ectoderm, through WNT7a, is required together with FGF4 to maintain Shh expression in the posterior mesenchyme. Removing that signal causes loss of posterior skeletal elements. This is the link from a dorsoventral signalling defect to the postaxial limb deficiencies seen clinically.

evidence.reference_title: Interaction between the signaling molecules WNT7a and SHH during vertebrate limb development: dorsal signals regulate anteroposterior patterning.
evidence.snippet: Wnt7a, which is expressed in dorsal ectoderm, provides the signal required for Shh expression and formation of posterior structures.

evidence.reference_title: Interaction between the signaling molecules WNT7a and SHH during vertebrate limb development: dorsal signals regulate anteroposterior patterning.
evidence.snippet: Removal of dorsal ectoderm results in loss of posterior skeletal elements, which can be rescued by exogenous SHH.

nodes.description: WNT7A from the dorsal ectoderm induces and maintains the LIM homeodomain transcription factor LMX1 in dorsal limb mesenchyme, which specifies dorsal identity. Weakened induction produces the dorsal-structure defects, including nail hypoplasia.
nodes.id: Impaired Dorsoventral Patterning of the Limb

evidence.reference_title: Induction of the LIM homeobox gene Lmx1 by WNT7a establishes dorsoventral pattern in the vertebrate limb.
evidence.snippet: Thus, the dorsalization of limb mesoderm appears to involve the WNT7a-mediated induction of Lmx1 in limb mesenchymal cells.

nodes.description: Hypoplastic or absent nails, reflecting the dorsalization defect.

evidence.reference_title: Induction of the LIM homeobox gene Lmx1 by WNT7a establishes dorsoventral pattern in the vertebrate limb.
evidence.snippet: Ectopic expression of Lmx1 in the ventral mesenchyme is sufficient to generate double-dorsal limbs.

nodes.description: Homozygous missense WNT7A variants reduce, but do not abolish, the activity of the secreted dorsal-ectoderm signal. The residual activity is what separates Fuhrmann syndrome from AARRS: null alleles of the same gene produce the much more severe phocomelia phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in WNT7A cause a range of limb malformations, including Fuhrmann syndrome and Al-Awadi/Raas-Rothschild/Schinzel phocomelia syndrome.
evidence.snippet: The results suggest that a partial loss of WNT7A function causes Fuhrmann syndrome (and a phenotype similar to mouse Wnt7a knockout), whereas the more-severe limb truncation phenotypes observed in Al-Awadi/Raas-Rothschild/Schinzel phocomelia syndrome result from null mutations (and cause a phenotype similar to mouse Shh knockout).

nodes.description: Absence or hypoplasia of the fibula with oligodactyly — the posterior skeletal elements this branch accounts for. Femoral bowing is deliberately not included: it is a proximal long-bone deformity, not a posterior element, and this branch does not explain it.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in WNT7A cause a range of limb malformations, including Fuhrmann syndrome and Al-Awadi/Raas-Rothschild/Schinzel phocomelia syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Fuhrmann syndrome and the Al-Awadi/Raas-Rothschild/Schinzel phocomelia syndrome are considered to be distinct limb-malformation disorders characterized by various degrees of limb aplasia/hypoplasia and joint dysplasia in humans.
